title: Retailers Hunt for the Next Big Beauty Superstar at Indie Beauty Expo
summary: Retailers like Ulta Beauty, HSN, Sephora, and Amazon attended the Indie Beauty Expo in Los Angeles to find emerging beauty brands. The expo showcased 102 budding brands to over a thousand attendees and 310 buyers, highlighting the significant growth of indie beauty brands in the market. Categories like color cosmetics, fragrance, skin care, and even oral care and ingestibles were featured, appealing to Millennial shoppers and those seeking natural beauty options.

title: Target cuts innovation initiatives, including secretive Goldfish start-up
summary: Target Corp. is scaling back its innovation initiatives, including the secretive e-commerce start-up Goldfish and a prototype for a robot-infused store of the future, due to declining sales and traffic during the holidays. This strategic shift aims to refocus efforts on the core business, leaving some within the company unsettled about long-term growth plans. The cutbacks follow a period of weakening sales performance and executive turnover, prompting analysts to suggest Target prioritizes fixing fundamental retail operations before extensive innovation.

title: Target’s Goldfish effort goes belly up amid shift to core business focus
summary: Target has refined its "innovation portfolio" by eliminating its Silicon Valley-based "Goldfish" startup and other tech initiatives to concentrate on its core business, both in stores and online. This decision follows executive changes and a challenging holiday sales period, despite healthy e-commerce growth, as the retailer aims to strengthen its brick-and-mortar fundamentals and strategic priorities. Target also lowered its Q4 and full-year 2016 guidance due to declining sales.

title: Human-Machine Relationship Key Theme Of Gartner Hype Cycle 2013
summary: Gartner's 2013 Hype Cycle for Emerging Technologies highlights the evolving relationship between humans and machines as its central theme, driven by increased hype around smart machines, cognitive computing, and the Internet of Things. The report identifies three main trends: augmenting humans with technology, machines replacing humans, and humans and machines working alongside each other. These trends are supported by technologies that enhance mutual understanding and intelligence between humans and machines.

title: What's New in PAN-OS 8.0 - Security Platform
summary: Palo Alto Networks introduced PAN-OS 8.0 with numerous enhancements to combat cyberattacks, focusing on securing multi-cloud environments and SaaS applications. Key features include improved prevention of credential theft, multi-method threat prevention with advanced WildFire service, and high-performance hardware. The update also streamlines security operations with centralized management and simplifies User-ID deployments for better access control.

title: Rackspace Lays Off 200 Locals in Companywide Cuts
summary: Rackspace Hosting Inc. announced the largest downsizing in its 19-year history, cutting 6% of its total U.S. workforce, which included 200 jobs at its Windcrest headquarters in San Antonio. This move is part of an effort to reduce spending by 7% companywide in 2017 following its acquisition by Apollo Global Management LLC, with a focus on preserving customer-facing roles and cutting positions primarily at the VP and director levels. Local leaders and organizations, including the City of San Antonio and Bexar County, are collaborating with Rackspace to provide outplacement services and connect displaced tech talent with other local companies.

title: CXA Group raises US$25 mil, on US$100 mil valuation, Eduardo Saverin joins board
summary: CXA Group, a Singapore-based health technology startup, announced a US$25 million Series B investment round, valuing the company at US$100 million. The funding, led by B Capital Group and EDBI, will facilitate expansion into ten new Asian markets, including China and India. Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin has joined CXA's board, and the company aims to double its revenue to US$14 million in 2017.

title: Can Amazon compete with O'Reilly Auto Parts? CEO responds to report
summary: O'Reilly Automotive CEO Greg Henslee expressed confidence in the company's position despite Amazon's aggressive expansion into the auto parts market. Henslee stated that O'Reilly's technical expertise, in-store professionals, and customer relationships for both DIY and professional mechanics provide a significant barrier to entry for online retailers. He believes that while Amazon might take some market share, it won't become a prominent competitor.

title: Gildan completes acquisition of American Apparel
summary: Gildan Activewear Inc. has completed its acquisition of the American Apparel brand and certain assets for $103 million, ending a bidding war that followed American Apparel's second Chapter 11 filing. Gildan, a Canadian apparel maker, outbid competitors like Amazon and Forever 21, adding American Apparel to its portfolio of brands. Future plans for the American Apparel brand under Gildan are expected to be announced with Gildan's upcoming quarterly earnings report.

title: Snapchat expected to invest $1 billion in Amazon cloud services
summary: Snap Inc., the owner of Snapchat, announced its intention to spend $1 billion over the next five years on Amazon.com Inc.'s cloud services, adding to an existing $2 billion contract with Google. The company also hinted at potentially building its own infrastructure in the future. This investment is part of Snapchat's preparations for its planned stock market debut in March, where it aims to raise $3 billion and could be valued between $20 billion and $25 billion.

title: Q&A: Hershey futurists discuss what’s next in retail
summary: Lina Yang and Brian Kavanagh, futurists at The Hershey Company, discuss emerging trends in food retail such as the shift from ingredient-based shopping to meal solutions and the importance of frictionless experiences. They highlight the impact of technology like Amazon Go's payment-free concept and the role of artificial intelligence in shaping the future of grocery shopping. Hershey's Medley concept store is presented as a storytelling tool to envision and spark discussions about the future of retail.

title: Wal-Mart coordinating e-commerce, brick-and-mortar supply operations
summary: Walmart is streamlining its buying efforts to boost its online assortment, allowing store buyers to purchase items for both physical stores and Walmart.com. This initiative aims to simplify the process for including in-store products in the online assortment, though e-commerce and brick-and-mortar buying teams will remain separate. This move is part of broader operational changes following the acquisition of Jet.com, focusing on expanding online selection and attracting new customers by offering free two-day shipping on orders over $35.

title: Fremont Technology Companies
summary: Fremont, often called the "Silicon Canal," is home to a concentration of technology companies in Seattle. This article lists several prominent tech firms located there, including Google, Adobe, and Getty Images, along with details about their operations. The list aims to showcase the diverse tech presence in the Fremont neighborhood.

title: New Amazon Stock Price Prediction Shows Shares Climbing to $900
summary: This article predicts Amazon's stock price will reach $900, driven by the shift from brick-and-mortar retail to e-commerce. It highlights Amazon's strong Q4 2016 earnings, revenue growth across its e-commerce and cloud divisions, and plans to hire 100,000 new employees as key indicators of continued expansion and bullish sentiment. The company's expansion into new product lines like groceries and clothing is also noted as a factor in its expected growth.

title: Blackstone Acquires AWS, Microsoft, Salesforce Cloud Partner Cloudreach
summary: Blackstone has acquired majority control of Cloudreach, an MSP and IT consulting firm specializing in migrations to AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Salesforce. Cloudreach, based in London, had £47.7 million in revenue for the 12 months ended July 2016 and plans to expand its geographic reach, software development, and managed services with Blackstone's backing. This acquisition is part of a growing trend of M&A deals involving AWS, Microsoft, and Salesforce partners.

title: Here’s Why Apple Isn’t Building an Amazon Echo Rival
summary: The article explains why Apple is not directly competing with Amazon's Echo device despite the success of voice-activated AI. Apple's strategy focuses on making Siri an omnipresent AI assistant across all its devices, rather than creating a dedicated smart speaker. The author argues this approach, exemplified by Siri's integration with AirPods and HomeKit, will prove more effective in the long run for winning the AI wars.

title: Array Technologies to supply trackers for Facebook solar plants in New Mexico
summary: Affordable Solar will utilize Array Technologies' DuraTrack HZ v3 trackers for three 10 MW-AC solar projects in New Mexico, which will supply power to Facebook's new data center. The $37 million contract was awarded by Public Service Company of New Mexico (PNM), and the solar plants are expected to help the data center achieve 100% renewable energy use. This deal highlights the growing trend of corporate renewable energy procurement through "Green Tariff" arrangements in regulated utility areas.

title: Exclusive: Apple expanding its Seattle engineering center, making a big bet on artificial intelligence
summary: Apple is significantly expanding its engineering operations in Seattle, with a focus on artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies for its products. The expansion is marked by a commitment to take additional floors at Two Union Square and is supported by Apple's acquisition of Seattle startup Turi, which also led to a new $1 million endowed professorship at the University of Washington. This move highlights Seattle's growing importance as a hub for AI development, attracting talent and investment from tech giants and startups alike.

title: FVAL Stock Price | Fidelity Value Factor ETF
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Fidelity Value Factor ETF (FVAL), including its current stock price, trading exchange (NYSE), and key financial statistics such as market capitalization, expense ratio, dividend yield, and inception date. It also lists top holdings and offers performance data, aiming to help investors assess FVAL's potential.

title: Nimble Storage debuts new cross-cloud data management service
summary: Nimble Storage Inc. has launched a new service called Nimble Cloud Volumes, designed to simplify migrating enterprise applications to the cloud by allowing workloads to access on-premises data without needing to relocate it. This service addresses the financial and control challenges associated with moving large datasets, particularly for sensitive information. Initially supporting Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure, the service costs 10 cents per gigabyte per month.

title: How Much Did Amazon Web Services Outage Cost Businesses?
summary: An Amazon Web Services (AWS) outage on the East Coast in February 2017 caused widespread disruption for thousands of businesses, including major services like Adobe, Twitch, and Slack. While AWS usually boasts high reliability, this incident highlighted the significant costs of downtime. IDC research indicates that AWS users generally experience far less downtime than those not using the service, resulting in substantial savings in lost productivity and revenue.

title: Nimble Storage wants to help companies avoid cloud vendor lock-in
summary: Nimble Storage has launched a new cloud storage service called Nimble Cloud Volumes to help enterprises navigate multi-cloud environments and prevent vendor lock-in. This service aims to enable seamless data migration between major cloud providers like AWS and Microsoft Azure, targeting core business applications with specific storage needs. The offering addresses the growing trend of multi-cloud strategies, which are now adopted by 85% of enterprises according to a recent survey.

title: JPMorgan software does in seconds what took lawyers 360,000 hours
summary: JPMorgan has developed "COIN" (Contract Intelligence) software to automate the parsing of financial deals, a task that previously required 360,000 hours of lawyer time annually. This initiative is part of a broader push by JPMorgan into automation and new technologies, driven by a $9.6 billion technology budget and fears of competition from startups. The bank aims to reduce expenses, create new revenue streams, and improve efficiency by leveraging machine learning, big data, and cloud infrastructure, while also making some of its technology available to institutional clients.

title: Site of Amazon’s cloud glitch made it especially disruptive
summary: A lengthy outage on Amazon's cloud storage service, S3, caused widespread disruptions in online services across many clients. The incident, stemming from the US-EAST-1 region, highlighted the critical reliance on cloud infrastructure and how glitches in large cloud providers like AWS can have a magnified impact due to their popularity and historical reliability. Experts believe the outage was likely a software-configuration problem and is unlikely to deter cloud adoption despite the initial shock.
